new_statements.quote: Las rallitas o asentos que pongo sobre de las vocales es para que se conosca en donde cae la fuerza de la pronunciación; y sí en un termino se ponen dos, es porque ambas son largas y con todo eso, esta lengua es mui violenta en su pronunciación. [Montoya 1789 apud Del Carpio-Penagos & Álvarez-Vázquez 2014: 215] || Accent is of the utmost importance in both these dialects ... The words for bird, snake and flower are the same; but Albornoz gives this very example to illustrate the importance of accent, nolō, a snake, nolô, a flower. Unfortunately, none of my authorities employ any accentual mark but the acute, and this appears to be syllabic. [Brinton 1886: 9]
new_statements.translation: The little strokes or accents that I put over the vowels are so that one may know where the force of the pronunciation falls; and if two are put on one word, it is because both [vowels] are long; and with all that, this language is very violent [forceful] in its pronunciation.
new_statements.citation: Montoya, Fray Francisco. 1789. [Vocabulario castellano-chiapaneca, Chiapa, 27 Feb 1789; AGI Documentos Escogidos 1, N165], transcribed in Del Carpio-Penagos, Carlos Uriel & Juan Ramón Álvarez-Vázquez. 2014. Vocabulario en lengua chiapaneca de fines del siglo XVIII. LiminaR 12(1): 212-230; supplemented by Brinton 1886, Notes on the Mangue, p. 9 (reporting Albornoz ca. 1690/1875).
new_statements.locator: Del Carpio-Penagos & Álvarez-Vázquez 2014, p. 215 (Montoya's 'advertencias'); accented vocabulary in cuadros 2-11, pp. 221-230. Brinton 1886 separate p. 9 (file, scan page 16).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: (1) Montoya 1789 note is verbatim at Del Carpio-Penagos & Alvarez-Vazquez 2014 p. 215 (saved text lines 162-168: 'Las rallitas o asentos que pongo sobre de las vocales es para que se conosca en donde cae la fuerza de la pronunciación; y sí en un termino se ponen dos, es porque ambas son largas y con todo eso, esta lengua es mui violenta en su pronunciación.'), inside Montoya's 'advertencias' addressed to the intendente, dated Chiapa 27 Feb 1789. (2) Brinton 1886 p. 9 passage is present in lines 468-475 ('Accent is of the utmost importance in both these dialects... Albornoz gives this very example to illustrate the importance of accent, no/o, a snake, nolo^ a flower. Unfortunate…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is stated anywhere. The only first-hand statements are (a) Montoya 1789: prominence ('fuerza de la pronunciación') is marked word by word with an accent, implying it was not felt to be predictable; in his list the mark sits on the final syllable in roughly two thirds of accented forms (188/278), on the penult in 65 and antepenult in 21, the non-final cases largely being stem-final before the endings -mu/-me/-hu; (b) Albornoz (ca. 1690, via Adam 1887/Brinton 1886/Müller 1888): an 'acento largo' vs 'acento breve' contrast on the same (final) vowel distinguishes lexical pairs (nolō 'snake' / nolô 'flower'), singular vs plural and 1st vs 3rd person, read by Müller as final-vowel quantity, i.e. a length/tone-type contrast rather than stress position. Net: colonial orthographic evidence points to word-final (stem-final) prominence plus a quantity/tonal contrast, but no source formulates a stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated (Montoya's double accent marks = 'ambas son largas', i.e. two long vowels, not secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; in Montoya's data forms ending in -mu, -me, -hu, -mo typically carry the accent on the preceding (stem-final) syllable (e.g. Cupúmu, Natúhmu, Charícame, Nitángame).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in an elicited 1789 word list (isolated words, many with nominal n-/na- prefixes and -mu/-me endings); Albornoz's acento pairs are word-level lexical/morphological contrasts. Language extinct since late 19th/early 20th c.; all evidence is philological.
new_statements.identity_note: All evidence is philological for extinct Chiapanec (chia1262, ISO cip) of Chiapa de Corzo/Suchiapa/Acala: Montoya's 1789 list was compiled at Chiapa (Chiapa de Corzo); Albornoz's Arte (ca. 1690) describes the same language. Brinton 1886 treats Chiapanec together with Mangue/Chorotega of Nicaragua (a separate Glottolog language), but the accent example he cites is Albornoz's Chiapanec.

sources.note: 'Die Laute' gives vowel/consonant inventory and phonotactics ('Der Auslaut ist stets vocalisch'); no accent/Betonung statement; interprets Albornoz's sg./pl. accent pairs as 'verschiedene Quantität des schliessenden Vocals'.

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1886. Notes on the Mangue; an extinct dialect formerly spoken in Nicaragua. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 23: 238-257 (separate print, Philadelphia 1886).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: p. 9 (separate): 'Accent is of the utmost importance in both these dialects [Mangue, Chapanec]... Albornoz gives this very example to illustrate the importance of accent, nolō, a snake, nolô, a flower.' The contrast is a diacritic on the same final vowel (Albornoz's acento largo vs breve), i.e. quantity/tone-like, not a statement of stress position.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1887. La langue chiapanèque: observations grammaticales, vocabulaire méthodique, textes inédits, textes rétablis. Vienne: Hölder.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: 'Phonétique' (pp. 1-2) covers letters and consonant mutations only; no stress-placement statement. Reports Albornoz's 'acento largo' (singular; 1st person) vs 'acento breve' (plural; 3rd person) as a morphological marker (pp. 6-7, 14-15: 'La première personne est indiquée par l'accent long... La troisième personne est indiquée par l'accent bref').

sources.citation: Del Carpio-Penagos, Carlos Uriel & Juan Ramón Álvarez-Vázquez. 2014. Vocabulario en lengua chiapaneca de fines del siglo XVIII. LiminaR. Estudios Sociales y Humanísticos 12(1): 212-230. DOI 10.29043/liminar.v12i1.333 (transcribes Fray Francisco Montoya's 1789 Castilian-Chiapanec vocabulary, AGI Documentos Escogidos 1, N165).
sources.note: p. 215 reproduces Montoya's 1789 note that his accent marks show 'en donde cae la fuerza de la pronunciación' (two marks = both vowels long); the accented word list (cuadros 2-11) shows the accent mostly on the final syllable (my tally: 188 of 278 accent-marked forms final, 65 penult, 21 antepenult; many non-final cases are stem-final before -mu/-me/-hu). No placement rule is stated.
